newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB expects margins to contract more.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB expects margins to contract more.

text.p: National Australia Bank said on Thursday that it expected interest margins to contract further in the near term.
"You're margins are going to continue under pressure, there's no doubt," said NAB managing director Don Argus.
"You're in a competitive game and I would expect that they will contract a little more yet," Argus told reporters.
Argus said thE bank aimed to get its cost to income ratio down to 40 percent by the year 2000.
"We're driving down to what we wish to get to by the year 2000, and that's somewhere down towards the 40 (percent) mark," Argus said.
Despite the short-term pressure on margins, Argus expected an uptick in the world economy during the second half of calendar 1997 which might feed through to the Australian economy.
"When you look out beyond, say June...there's a chance that you'll get an uptick in the economy here in the second half of the year," he said.
NAB earlier on Thursday announced a 13.5 percent rise in net profit to A$582 million for the three months to December 31.

The bank said earlier that interest margins remained under pressure in all markets but that the group's strong focus on business fundamentals and its international spread of banking and financial services augured well for the future.
National Australia Bank shares were 39 cents higher at A$15.40 at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT) on Thursday.
